question: What does AWS Control Tower create and apply when it sets up a landing zone, and what changed in landing zone version 4.0?
claim: When it sets up a landing zone through the console, Control Tower creates the Security OU and an optional Sandbox OU, creates an IAM Identity Center directory (or lets you self-manage your identity provider), and applies all mandatory preventive and detective controls; starting with landing zone version 4.0, mandatory controls are no longer applied by default.

qualifiers.scope: landing zone set up through the console
qualifiers.condition: starting with landing zone version 4.0, mandatory controls are no longer applied by default

evidence.quote: When you create your landing zone through the console, AWS Control Tower creates two AWS Organizations organizational units (OUs). These are the Security OU and the optional Sandbox OU, contained within the organizational root structure.

Creates a cloud-native directory in IAM Identity Center, with preconfigured groups and single sign-on access, if you choose the default AWS Control Tower configuration, or it allows you to self-manage your identity provider.
Applies all mandatory, preventive controls to enforce policies.
Applies all mandatory, detective controls to detect configuration violations.
Starting with AWS Control Tower Landing Zone version 4.0, mandatory controls are no longer applied by default.
